newsitem.title: USA: Piper calls remaining litigation manageable.
newsitem.headline: Piper calls remaining litigation manageable.

text.p: Piper Jaffray Cos Inc, a regional brokerage house, said Wednesday it believes its remaining litigation exposure related to Piper Capital Management is "manageable."
Litigation has been brought on behalf of holders of several Piper Capital funds or assets managed by Piper Capital.
Previous settlements, on a net basis, amounted to $56.1 million in fiscal 1995 and $29.5 million in fiscal 1996.
Piper Jaffray said it is cooperating in regulatory investigations being conducted by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and other regulatory agencies, as previously reported.
It also repeated that, because it is impossible to predict the outcome of these actions, no provision for any loss that may result has been recorded in its financial statements.
It added that the aggregate cost of litigation and any judgments or settlements could have a material adverse effect on its consolidated financial statements.
Piper also said it has a team working toward resolution of these issues, while focusing on managing its business, building client relationships and attracting new clients.

Piper Jaffray reported earnings for the fourth quarter ended September 30 of $0.24 a sahre, down from $0.30 a year ago. Quarterly revenues were $136.2 million, up from $132.2 million. Revenues for the year were a record $553.9 million, up from $431.7 million a year ago.

"We continued to strengthen our presence in the markets in which we do business, and took advantage of opportunities provided by the strong but volatile stock and bond markets," Addison Piper, chairman, said in a statement.

Piper said Individual Investor Services revenue topped its fiscal 1995 record by 29 percent to reach $358.9 million for fiscal 1996. Equity Capital Markets brought 51 offerings to market during fiscal 1996, an increase of 55 percent, Piper said, while the industry total rose 49 percent.

During fiscal 1996 Fixed Income Capital Markets managed or co-managed 634 negotiated, competitive and advisory issues totaling $8.3 billion. That compares with 552 issues totaling $5.9 billion in fiscal 1995.
